steps: 1. Download the supplementary PDF file with curl.

2. Run 'pdftotext -layout raw/spalding2017_mmc1.pdf raw/sp_layout.txt'. The layout mode keeps the eight columns apart. The plain mode breaks the table into one token per line and was not used for the values.
3. Select the text between the row 'Anguilla' and the row 'Virgin Islands (U.S.)'.

4. On each line, match the last seven fields with the regular expression '(?:\$?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?%?|n/a)'. The text before the first match is the country name. A line with fewer than seven matches and no digit is a wrapped country name; the parser holds that text and joins it to the next line. This recovers 'St. Vincent and the Grenadines'.
5. Strip the dollar sign, the comma and the percent sign from each value. Map 'n/a' to an empty cell.
6. Write the CSV file with pandas.
extraction_method.parser_defect_found_and_fixed: The first version of the regular expression allowed a bare comma as a numeric token. That version cut 'Bahamas, The' down to 'Bahamas' and cut four other names. The fix requires at least one digit. The analyst confirmed all 80 names after the fix.
